# Kestrel Gwilham

Kestrel Gwilham is an Interconnection Queue Analyst at Zordra Robotics, specializing in the management and approval of large-scale battery storage projects within complex grid interconnection processes. Since joining Zordra in early 2022, Kestrel has contributed to the FluxCore dispatch software, which automates battery dispatch decisions to optimize both asset lifespan and revenue streams.

Prior to Zordra, Kestrel worked for three years at GridLink Solutions (2018–2021), where they led a key initiative to streamline queue prioritization for projects exceeding 500MW capacity. This involved developing a proprietary risk scoring model under the internal codename “Project FalconEye,” which reduced average approval times by 30% and improved forecast accuracy for interconnection timelines.

Kestrel’s expertise lies at the intersection of grid-scale battery storage technology, regulatory compliance, and data-driven decision-making within interconnection queues. They are particularly skilled in navigating the complex interdependencies between battery degradation modeling and dispatch optimization to ensure projects meet stringent operational and financial criteria.

Known for a meticulous, analytical working style, Kestrel collaborates closely with system operators, regulatory analysts, and software engineers. Their work has been integral to cross-team projects like “PulseTrack,” a collaborative effort to integrate real-time queue data into dispatch algorithms, enhancing the overall efficiency of large battery deployments on the grid.

Current employer: [[companies/zordra-robotics]].
